method: multi-seed (>=5 seeds) x two p; syndrome-memoized coset-ML; CI-aware trend kill-switch (pooled-Wilson-propagated ratio CI)

bb_spine_selection.criterion: strong bivariate: A and B each mix x and y
strong bivariate: A and B each mix x and y
strong bivariate: A and B each mix x and y

methodology_validation.issue: the ORIGINAL trend kill-switch was a strict point-estimate rule (fire C on any strictly-increasing BB ratio sequence). At these scales all BB ratios sit in a ~1% sampling-noise band around 1.0, so a monotone ordering can arise from RNG noise alone -> the rule was a noise detector and could flip the decisive label by seed.

counterexample.note: strictly increasing by sampling noise alone; every ratio ~1.0 within CI

methodology_validation.resolution: TREND switch is now CI-aware (fires only if BB ratios strictly increase AND the largest-n ratio_lo > smallest-n ratio_hi, i.e. growth exceeds sampling noise), applied to MULTI-SEED pooled ratios. LEVEL switch unchanged (strict ratio>2.0; 2x is ~100 sigma outside the noise band, so it needs no CI-awareness).

0.05.reason: all gaps <=2x and no significant increasing BB trend (CI-aware)

0.01.reason: all gaps <=2x and no significant increasing BB trend (CI-aware)
